name: Lettuce
grown_as: A hearting lettuce cut whole, drawn as a butterhead: a round head of soft, smooth leaves. William's records list several lettuces ('Marvel of Four Seasons', a butterhead with red-bronze outer leaves; 'Bronze Arrow', an oakleaf; Lollo rosso and blonda; a loose-leaf cutting mix), so the look depends on which is meant. Drawn green as the most typical. ⚠️ CHECK which lettuce the drawing should be.
habit: A low rosette 20 to 30 cm across and 10 to 20 cm high on a very short stem hidden at its centre. The inner leaves fold over each other into a round, loose head. When it bolts the stem shoots up from the middle to 60 to 100 cm and branches at the top.

leaf.arrangement: A tight rosette, the leaves spiralling round a short central stem
leaf.outline: Broad and rounded to obovate (widest above the middle), 10 to 20 cm long and nearly as wide, cupped
leaf.base: Narrowing into a broad, flat, pale midrib; no separate stalk
leaf.margin: Smooth, without teeth, gently wavy and a little crimped at the edge
leaf.veins: A broad pale midrib, widest at the base; side veins fanning out and branching into a fine net, pale and slightly raised
leaf.surface: Soft, thin, smooth and hairless, softly puckered between the veins; not glossy
leaf.stalk: None: the widened midrib does the work of a stalk
leaf.colour: Fresh mid green, the heart paler yellow-green; red-flushed outer leaves in some varieties

flower.form: A small head like a little dandelion, made only of strap-shaped florets, opening flat in the morning and closing by midday
flower.petals: No true petals to count: about 10 to 25 strap-shaped florets, each a single ray with five tiny teeth across its squared-off tip, laid out like the rays of a dandelion
flower.centre: No separate eye: the inner florets are shorter and the forked yellow styles stand up in the middle
flower.behind: A slim cylindrical cup (involucre) of narrow green bracts overlapping like roof tiles, longer than wide, sometimes tinged purple
flower.carried: Many heads on short stalks in a wide, branched, flat-topped spray at the top of a tall bolted stem, the heads facing up
flower.season: July to September, after the plant bolts

fruit: Each floret makes one seed (achene): slim, flattened, 3 to 4 mm, with fine lengthwise ribs, narrowing at the top into a thin beak carrying a tuft of soft white hairs (pappus). Seed colour is white-cream, grey, brown or black depending on variety. The heads open into small white fluffy clocks, much smaller and looser than a dandelion clock. The plant has milky sap.
seedling: Two smooth, oval to spoon-shaped seed leaves about 1 cm long on short stalks, then rounded true leaves with softly wavy edges, one at a time, forming a little rosette.
winter: Nothing: grown as an annual. Hardy winter varieties stay as small rosettes under cover.

leaf: a broad rounded blade with no separate stalk, narrowing into a wide pale midrib
smooth wavy edge with no teeth
side veins fanning from the midrib, the surface softly puckered

seedling: the first true leaf rounded, softly wavy
young: a loose rosette of broad rounded leaves flat to the soil
crop: a round head of leaves folded over a paler heart

look_alikes: Prickly lettuce (Lactuca serriola) is the wild relative: a row of prickles under the midrib and leaves often turned edge-on to the sun. Endive and chicory have blue flowers and bitter leaves. Sow-thistles have spiny-edged, clasping leaves and larger yellow heads.
